lineage_context.teaching_goal: Recognize the one-whorl petaloid perianth and anthocarp as a distinct Caryophyllales reproductive solution.

project_scope.selection_mode: Central Texas family-first module centered on anthocarp structure and four local/project genera
project_scope.note: What looks like a corolla is usually the petaloid upper portion of a single perianth whorl; a separate true corolla is absent.

family_diagnostics.where_to_look_first: Look for a tubular or funnelform petaloid perianth with no separate corolla, often subtended by an involucre of bracts. Then follow the flower into fruit: the persistent basal perianth encloses the one-seeded fruit to form an anthocarp.
family_diagnostics.vegetative: Herbs, shrubs, trees or climbers; leaves simple, usually opposite or alternate, without stipules.
family_diagnostics.reproductive: Flowers bisexual or unisexual, usually with one petaloid perianth whorl. Bracts may form a calyx-like involucre. Ovary superior, one-celled, one-ovuled.
family_diagnostics.fruit: An indehiscent one-seeded fruit enclosed by the persistent enlarged perianth base—the anthocarp—which may be ribbed, winged, tuberculate or glandular.
family_diagnostics.field_tip: Family door: no true corolla + petaloid perianth + anthocarp. The anthocarp is the structure worth learning.

visual_lesson.teaching_order: petaloid perianth → involucre → anthocarp → genus doors → close-family comparison
visual_lesson.intro: In Nyctaginaceae, the showy 'petals' are not petals. Learn the single petaloid perianth and the anthocarp and the whole family suddenly becomes coherent.

steps.title: 1 · Notice there is no separate corolla
steps.look_for: A colorful tubular/funnelform perianth that performs the visual job of a corolla, but there is only one perianth whorl.
steps.why_it_matters: This immediately separates the family from Caryophyllaceae's typical sepals + petals.

steps.title: 2 · Follow the perianth base into the anthocarp
steps.look_for: The upper petaloid part withers/falls, while the lower perianth persists and enlarges tightly around the one-seeded fruit.
steps.why_it_matters: The anthocarp is the family's strongest reproductive concept.

steps.title: 3 · Mirabilis door: calyx-like involucre
steps.look_for: Five bracts commonly fused into a calyx-like involucre, with one or several flowers; mature anthocarps are usually ribbed or tuberculate.
steps.why_it_matters: Mirabilis is the best-known four-o'clock architecture.

steps.title: 4 · Boerhavia door: tiny flowers, ribbed/glandular anthocarps
steps.look_for: Relatively small flowers in clusters and narrow fruits/anthocarps with prominent ribs, sometimes glandular.
steps.why_it_matters: Boerhavia is easy to miss until you learn the fruit.

steps.title: 5 · Acleisanthes/Allionia doors
steps.photo_role: long tubular Acleisanthes flower / Allionia cluster and fruit
steps.look_for: Acleisanthes often has relatively large solitary long-tubed flowers and some species have winged anthocarps; Allionia combines magenta clustered flowers with distinctive glandular/winged fruit surfaces.
steps.why_it_matters: Fruit shape and anthocarp ornamentation do much of the genus-level work.

comparisons.title: Nyctaginaceae vs Caryophyllaceae
comparisons.rule: Nyctaginaceae lacks a separate true corolla and makes an anthocarp around a one-seeded fruit. Caryophyllaceae usually has distinct sepals + petals and a many-seeded capsule.

comparisons.title: Nyctaginaceae vs Amaranthaceae
comparisons.rule: Both can have one perianth whorl and one-seeded fruits. Nyctaginaceae typically has a more obviously petaloid tubular perianth whose base becomes an anthocarp; Amaranthaceae emphasizes tiny papery bracteate flowers.

comparisons.title: Nyctaginaceae vs Phytolaccaceae
comparisons.rule: Both may lack a separate corolla. Nyctaginaceae usually has a fused petaloid perianth and anthocarp enclosing a single fruit; Phytolaccaceae does not use the anthocarp architecture.

visual_lesson.caveat: Do not call the showy perianth 'petals' in the botanical lesson. Also do not treat opposite leaves as universal; leaf arrangement varies.

genera.fast_cue: calyx-like involucre + funnelform petaloid perianth + ribbed anthocarp
tiny clustered flowers + strongly ribbed/glandular anthocarps
often large solitary long-tubed flowers; some winged anthocarps
magenta clustered flowers + distinctive glandular/winged anthocarp
